title: Logistic regression, predicting yes or no

sentences.text: Purpose.
sentences.say: Purpose.

sentences.text: Many business questions have a yes or no answer: will this customer repay, accept the offer, churn?
sentences.say: Many business questions have a yes or no answer: will this customer repay, accept the offer, churn?

sentences.text: Logistic regression is the standard first model for them.
sentences.say: Logistic regression is the standard first model for them.

sentences.text: It is easy to explain, hard to beat as a baseline, and it is also the building block of neural networks.
sentences.say: It is easy to explain, hard to beat as a baseline, and it is also the building block of neural networks.

sentences.text: Key ideas
sentences.say: Key ideas

sentences.text: Despite its name, logistic regression is a classification model.
sentences.say: Despite its name, logistic regression is a classification model.

sentences.text: It outputs a probability between 0 and 1.
sentences.say: It outputs a probability between 0 and 1.

sentences.text: It takes the same weighted sum as linear regression, z = w . x + b, and squeezes it through the sigmoid function.
sentences.say: It takes the same weighted sum as linear regression, z equals w dot x plus b, and squeezes it through the sigmoid function.

sentences.text: The decision boundary is where z = 0, which is where the probability is 0.5.
sentences.say: The decision boundary is where z equals 0, which is where the probability is 0.5.

sentences.text: The 0.5 cut-off is a choice, not a law.
sentences.say: The 0.5 cut-off is a choice, not a law.

sentences.text: You can move it.
sentences.say: You can move it.

sentences.text: 9.1 Why not a straight line?
sentences.say: 9.1 Why not a straight line?

sentences.text: Ng's example is a tumour that is benign (0) or malignant (1), predicted from its size.
sentences.say: Ng's example is a tumour that is benign (0) or malignant (1), predicted from its size.

sentences.text: You could fit a straight line to those 0s and 1s and call anything above 0.5 malignant.
sentences.say: You could fit a straight line to those 0s and 1s and call anything above 0.5 malignant.

sentences.text: It works on tidy data, but it breaks for two reasons (Ng, video 31):
sentences.say: It works on tidy data, but it breaks for two reasons (Ng, video 31):

sentences.text: Add one very large tumour far to the right.
sentences.say: Add one very large tumour far to the right.

sentences.text: The line tilts to chase it, the 0.5 crossing moves, and some tumours that were classified correctly are now wrong.
sentences.say: The line tilts to chase it, the 0.5 crossing moves, and some tumours that were classified correctly are now wrong.

sentences.text: One outlier should not rewrite your rule.
sentences.say: One outlier should not rewrite your rule.

sentences.text: The line produces numbers like -0.4 and 1.7.
sentences.say: The line produces numbers like -0.4 and 1.7.

sentences.text: They are not probabilities and mean nothing.
sentences.say: They are not probabilities and mean nothing.

sentences.text: We need a curve that stays between 0 and 1 and flattens at both ends.
sentences.say: We need a curve that stays between 0 and 1 and flattens at both ends.

sentences.text: 9.2 The sigmoid
sentences.say: 9.2 The sigmoid

sentences.text: For a very large z the sigmoid is close to 1.
sentences.say: For a very large z the sigmoid is close to 1.

sentences.text: For a very large negative z it is close to 0.
sentences.say: For a very large negative z it is close to 0.

sentences.text: At z = 0 it is exactly 0.5.
sentences.say: At z equals 0 it is exactly 0.5.
Some values: g(-3) equals 0.047, g(-1) equals 0.269, g(0) equals 0.5, g(1) equals 0.731, g(3) equals 0.953.

sentences.text: Read the model's output as a probability: if f(x) = 0.7, the model says there is a 70% chance that y = 1 for this input (and so a 30% chance that y = 0).
sentences.say: Read the model's output as a probability: if f(x) equals 0.7, the model says there is a 70 percent chance that y equals 1 for this input (and so a 30 percent chance that y equals 0).

sentences.text: 9.3 The decision boundary
sentences.say: 9.3 The decision boundary

sentences.text: To turn the probability into a yes or no, use a threshold, usually 0.5.
sentences.say: To turn the probability into a yes or no, use a threshold, usually 0.5.

sentences.text: The sigmoid is at least 0.5 exactly when z is at least 0, so the model predicts 1 when w . x + b is at least 0.
sentences.say: The sigmoid is at least 0.5 exactly when z is at least 0, so the model predicts 1 when w dot x plus b is at least 0.

sentences.text: The set of inputs where w . x + b = 0 is the decision boundary: a line when there are two features.
sentences.say: The set of inputs where w dot x plus b equals 0 is the decision boundary: a line when there are two features.

sentences.text: Take w = [1, 1] and b = -3.
sentences.say: Take w equals 1, 1 and b equals -3.

sentences.text: The boundary is x1 + x2 = 3.
sentences.say: The boundary is x1 plus x2 equals 3.

sentences.text: Straight boundaries are not the limit.
sentences.say: Straight boundaries are not the limit.

sentences.text: If you feed the model squared features, such as x1 squared and x2 squared (Chapter 8), then with weights 1 and 1 and b = -1 the boundary x1 squared + x2 squared = 1 is a circle: points inside are class 0, points outside class 1.
sentences.say: If you feed the model squared features, such as x1 squared and x2 squared (Chapter 8), then with weights 1 and 1 and b equals -1 the boundary x1 squared plus x2 squared equals 1 is a circle: points inside are class 0, points outside class 1.

sentences.text: The model is still logistic regression; only the features changed.
sentences.say: The model is still logistic regression; only the features changed.

sentences.text: 9.4 Odds and log-odds
sentences.say: 9.4 Odds and log-odds

sentences.text: Beyond the videos (this is the statistician's view, as in StatQuest).
sentences.say: Beyond the videos (this is the statistician's view, as in StatQuest).

sentences.text: The odds of an event are p divided by (1 - p): a probability of 0.8 is odds of 4 to 1.
sentences.say: The odds of an event are p divided by (1 minus p): a probability of 0.8 is odds of 4 to 1.

sentences.text: The logarithm of the odds is the log-odds (or logit): ln 4 = 1.386.
sentences.say: The logarithm of the odds is the log-odds (or logit): ln 4 equals 1.386.

sentences.text: Here is the neat fact: z = w . x + b is exactly the log-odds.
sentences.say: Here is the neat fact: z equals w dot x plus b is exactly the log-odds.

sentences.text: Logistic regression is linear regression on the log-odds, and the sigmoid just turns log-odds back into a probability.
sentences.say: Logistic regression is linear regression on the log-odds, and the sigmoid just turns log-odds back into a probability.

sentences.text: This gives you a way to read the weights: each increase of 1 in feature j multiplies the odds by e to the power w_j.
sentences.say: This gives you a way to read the weights: each increase of 1 in feature j multiplies the odds by e to the power w j.

sentences.text: A weight of 0.5 multiplies the odds by 1.649, so "4 to 1" becomes about "6.6 to 1", all else equal.
sentences.say: A weight of 0.5 multiplies the odds by 1.649, so "4 to 1" becomes about "6.6 to 1", all else equal.

sentences.text: 9.5 The threshold is a choice
sentences.say: 9.5 The threshold is a choice

sentences.text: The default 0.5 treats both mistakes as equally bad.
sentences.say: The default 0.5 treats both mistakes as equally bad.

sentences.text: In lending they are not.
sentences.say: In lending they are not.

sentences.text: Approving a loan that defaults costs far more than declining a good applicant.
sentences.say: Approving a loan that defaults costs far more than declining a good applicant.

sentences.text: You can lower the threshold to flag more risky cases (catching more bad loans, with more false alarms) or raise it to be stricter.
sentences.say: You can lower the threshold to flag more risky cases (catching more bad loans, with more false alarms) or raise it to be stricter.

sentences.text: Chapter 12 shows how to choose with numbers.
sentences.say: Chapter 12 shows how to choose with numbers.

sentences.text: 9.6 More than two classes
sentences.say: 9.6 More than two classes

sentences.text: Beyond the videos.
sentences.say: Beyond the videos.

sentences.text: With more than two classes (the Gmail tabs example) the sigmoid is replaced by the softmax function.
sentences.say: With more than two classes (the Gmail tabs example) the sigmoid is replaced by the softmax function.

sentences.text: It turns one score per class into probabilities that add up to 1.
sentences.say: It turns one score per class into probabilities that add up to 1.

sentences.text: You will meet it again as the last layer of most neural networks.
sentences.say: You will meet it again as the last layer of most neural networks.

sentences.text: Loan example.
sentences.say: Loan example.

sentences.text: The probability that an offer is accepted is the sigmoid of w1 x amount + w2 x terms + w3 x credit score + b. A probability of 0.83 means "about 83 of 100 offers like this are accepted".
sentences.say: The probability that an offer is accepted is the sigmoid of w1 times amount plus w2 times terms plus w3 times credit score plus b. A probability of 0.83 means "about 83 of 100 offers like this are accepted".

sentences.text: You can rank offers by it, or turn it into a decision with a threshold, and a customer-facing explanation can use the weights: a larger amount lowers the odds of acceptance by a certain factor.
sentences.say: You can rank offers by it, or turn it into a decision with a threshold, and a customer-facing explanation can use the weights: a larger amount lowers the odds of acceptance by a certain factor.

sentences.text: Common mistakes
sentences.say: Common mistakes

sentences.text: Using linear regression on a 0 or 1 target.
sentences.say: Using linear regression on a 0 or 1 target.

sentences.text: Thinking the model output is a certainty.
sentences.say: Thinking the model output is a certainty.

sentences.text: It is a probability, and only as good as its calibration (Chapter 12).
sentences.say: It is a probability, and only as good as its calibration (Chapter 12).

sentences.text: Treating 0.5 as sacred.
sentences.say: Treating 0.5 as sacred.
